text:
Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, Monday, directed the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority, NCAA, to enforce full compliance with the Airport Passenger Verification System, vPASS, among all scheduled domestic airlines by December 31, saying passengers without a valid National Identification Number, NIN, will be barred from boarding domestic flights from January 1, 2027.
Keyamo said the initiative, approved by the Federal Executive Council, FEC, under President Bola Tinubu’s airport modernisation drive, was designed to eliminate airport touting, bulk ticket racketeering and identity fraud.
He spoke during the official unveiling of the vPASS at the Murtala Muhammed Airport, MMA, Domestic Terminal in Lagos.
He said: “I am giving the airlines till the end of December. I repeat it again: from January 1, no airline will be allowed to board their passengers if they don’t key into vPASS. All airlines, irrespective of whom, irrespective of whatever, must key into vPASS for scheduled flights.
“The vPASS is simply a system that is linked to all our NINs, so you cannot board any aircraft locally without your NIN. In one fell swoop, it has eliminated touting at the airport where people who have no business boarding aircraft get access to the departure lounge, or buy tickets in bulk and sell to people in other names. We now have clean manifests for all aircraft, and we know the clear identity of those who board.”
vPASS, developed by the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria, FAAN, in partnership with private-sector technology firm VERXID Technologies Limited, would be replacing the traditional physical identity checks and boarding-gate bottlenecks with contactless facial and iris biometric recognition.
Under the new protocol, Nigerian travellers must link their NIN and date of birth to their biometric profiles, either through the vPASS mobile application, available on the Google Play Store and Apple App Store, or at designated airport onboarding kiosks. Foreign nationals travelling on domestic routes will complete the onboarding process using their international passports.
Keyamo said the system would apply strictly to domestic operations, adding that a separate border-control framework had already been deployed at international terminals in collaboration with the Ministry of Interior.
On concerns that the public-private partnership could lead to additional costs for passengers, the minister assured travellers that any associated charge would be “very, very minimal.”
Speaking after demonstrating live registration alongside the minister, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of FAAN, Olubunmi Kuku, said the platform introduced a seamless “single sign-on” experience that strengthened terminal access control while accelerating passenger processing.
Kuku said: “Once you register, before you get into the security gates, you simply enter the last four digits of your NIN and it opens the gates for you. When you get to the airline boarding gates, instead of someone checking different forms of physical ID, you just use your facial biometrics or the QR code on your boarding pass. It is swift, smart, and efficient.”
Kuku confirmed that the infrastructure was already operational in Lagos and Abuja ahead of its nationwide expansion to all domestic airports.
She added that the remainder of November and the December Yuletide travel period would serve as an onboarding and pilot window for travellers before mandatory enforcement takes effect on January 1.
Highlighting the technical architecture behind the deployment, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of VERXID Technologies Limited, Adebayo Bankole, said the platform was built to meet strict data governance and operational standards.
Bankole said: “Our sole responsibility is to ensure the implementation is seamlessly put together, that passenger data security is well protected in full alignment with Nigeria’s data protection laws, and that travellers enjoy a frictionless experience across the airport ecosystem.”
